svg.title: Mena-LAM-6 on crystals and surfaces: accuracy, speed and memory
svg.desc: Matbench Discovery CPS accuracy, Silicon E+F+S throughput, and DynaMat v1.0 MD wall time and peak GPU memory for Mena-LAM-6 compared with published models.
svg.text: Default materials model (strict FP32). Matbench Discovery: CPS 0.874, F1 0.904, κSRME 0.182 (0/103 imaginary modes).
Combined Performance Score across discovery, geometry, and thermal conductivity (higher is better; training GPU-hours in parentheses)
Atoms per millisecond (higher is better): Mena-LAM-6 in strict FP32 vs. published models on 80–96 GB datacenter GPUs
DynaMat MD wall time and peak GPU memory
17 crystals × 80,000 NVT steps (210M atom-steps): the 14 models reporting peak VRAM, fastest first (lower is better).
Mena-LAM-6 (lam6-v1): CPS 0.874 in 48.5 single-GPU hours; WBM-257k relaxed in 4m 38s; DynaMat MD in 43.6 min (0.46 GB VRAM, CMDS 0.777).
On an Apple M3 Max laptop: 98.6 atoms/ms on Si 8k and 37.7 atoms/ms (0.049 MB/atom) on dense diamond 32k (158 neighbours/atom).
Baselines: Matbench Discovery leaderboard & FACTO Table 1 (EqV3/eSEN/Prophet run out of memory at 8k Si on 80–96 GB GPUs).
